brock_mirman.log_policy: khat' = alpha khat + z, exactly linear
brock_mirman.note: delta=1 with log utility is exactly log-linear, so every second-order term and the risk correction are zero.  The benchmark cannot show perturbation error -- which is why 5.A6 moves to the quarterly model.

certainty_equivalence.claim: c_chi = k_chi = 0: the shock scale enters no first-order coefficient.  Measured in key 'higher_order' as first_order_coeff_shift -- what adding the whole second-order block does to the four linear coefficients.

pert_first_order.matching_note: two independent routes to the same four numbers: generalized Schur on the linearized system, and root-finding on F=0, F_k=0, F_z=0

blanchard_kahn.rule: unique iff (# generalized eigenvalues outside the unit circle) = (# non-predetermined variables)
blanchard_kahn.method: generalized Schur (QZ) with stable eigenvalues ordered first; Klein (2000).  scipy.linalg.ordqz.

higher_order.conditions: F=0, F_k=0, F_z=0, F_kk=0, F_kz=0, F_zz=0, each a 2-vector
higher_order.reading: the risk correction scales with sigma^2: ten times the shock is a hundred times the correction

pruning.rule: Kim, Kim, Schaumburg & Sims (2008): propagate the first-order state, and feed only first-order terms into the second-order correction, so no term above the approximation order is ever squared.
pruning.reference: Andreasen, Fernandez-Villaverde & Rubio-Ramirez (2018) for the general pruned state-space and its moments.

projection_residual.model: Brock-Mirman, deterministic, delta=1; exact policy k' = alpha beta k^alpha
projection_residual.basis: Chebyshev in k, collocation at the Chebyshev nodes
projection_residual.point: the residual is a FUNCTION, not a number.  Collocation makes it exactly zero at n+1 points and leaves it free in between; more coefficients push the whole curve down.

basis_conditioning.gibbs_convention: the textbook 8.95% is measured against the JUMP (here 2); against the half-amplitude (here 1) the same number is 17.9%
basis_conditioning.note: the Hilbert matrix IS the least-squares normal matrix for monomials on [0,1]; its condition number is why the basis fails long before the approximation theory does

chebyshev.nodes: x_j = cos((2j-1)pi / 2n), the roots of T_n
chebyshev.interpolation_theorem: Chebyshev-node interpolation is within a factor (2/pi)log(n+1)+1 of the best possible polynomial of that degree
chebyshev.reading: analytic: error falls geometrically.  kinked: it falls like 1/n. The basis is not the problem -- the function is.

refinements: p: raise the degree inside each element
fem.note: compact support is the whole point: basis i and basis j overlap only if they share an element, so the assembled matrix is banded

collocation.quadrature: Gauss-Legendre, 40 nodes, for every integral condition
collocation.reading: collocation zeroes the residual at points; Galerkin zeroes its projection on the basis; least squares minimises it in L2.  Same unknowns, same basis, different senses of 'small'.

worked_proj.warm_start: first-order perturbation coefficients, fitted at the Chebyshev nodes

three_methods.model: quarterly RBC, Rouwenhorst 7 states, k in [0.5 k*, 1.5 k*]

_meta.calibration: quarterly RBC, Quant_Macro Lab7 (Block A theory and Block B use the Brock-Mirman delta=1 benchmark where a closed form is needed)
_meta.smolyak: NOT recomputed here -- 5.B3 reuses key 'smolyak' from tools/figures/s04_numbers.json, per slides/SOURCES.md

fig_monomials.note: normalized inner product of x^10 and x^11 under <f,g> = int_0^1 f g dx
